title: BPP lies in the second-level classes
statement: Let $E$ be a verifier model closed under polynomially many repetitions followed by majority vote, under negating a verifier's answer, and under the shift-or construction. If a language $L$ has a polynomial-time randomized verifier that uses polynomially many random bits and answers correctly with probability at least $2/3$ on every input, then $L$ belongs to both the second-level existential and universal polynomial-hierarchy classes defined using polynomial-length witnesses and polynomial-time predicates.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ is closed under majority repetition for the specified polynomial repetition counts
$E$ is closed under negating verifier answers
$E$ is closed under the shift-or construction
$L$ has an $E$-efficient Boolean verifier with polynomially bounded randomness and success probability at least $2/3$ on both yes and no inputs
